statement: Square $ABCD$ has side length $12$. Point $E$ lies on $\overline{BC}$ with $BE = 4$, and $F$ is the midpoint of $\overline{CD}$. Segment $\overline{AE}$ meets diagonal $\overline{BD}$ at $P$, and segment $\overline{AF}$ meets $\overline{BD}$ at $Q$. What is the area of triangle $APQ$?

choices.misconception: I assumed $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{AF}$ cut the diagonal $\overline{BD}$ into three equal parts, so $P$ and $Q$ were the trisection points.
I found triangle $AEF$ has area $60$ and shrank only side $\overline{AF}$ by $AQ/AF = \tfrac23$, leaving $\overline{AE}$ at full length.
I found triangle $AEF$ has area $60$ and shrank only side $\overline{AE}$ by $AP/AE = \tfrac34$, leaving $\overline{AF}$ at full length.
I found the area of triangle $AEF$, which is the larger triangle containing $APQ$, not triangle $APQ$ itself.

hints: Look for similar triangles with the diagonal: $\overline{AD} \parallel \overline{BC}$ and $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$.
Triangles $PBE$ and $PDA$ are similar, and so are $QDF$ and $QBA$. Their side ratios tell you what fraction of $\overline{AE}$ is $\overline{AP}$, and of $\overline{AF}$ is $\overline{AQ}$.
$AP : PE = AD : BE = 3 : 1$ and $AQ : QF = AB : DF = 2 : 1$. Then $[APQ] = \tfrac34 \cdot \tfrac23 \cdot [AEF]$.

solutions.reliable: Put $A = (0,0)$, $B = (12,0)$, $C = (12,12)$, $D = (0,12)$, so $E = (12,4)$ and $F = (6,12)$. Diagonal $\overline{BD}$ is $x + y = 12$. Line $AE$ is $y = x/3$, meeting it at $P = (9,3)$. Line $AF$ is $y = 2x$, meeting it at $Q = (4,8)$. The shoelace formula gives $[APQ] = \tfrac12 |9 \cdot 8 - 3 \cdot 4| = \tfrac12 \cdot 60 = 30$. Transferable idea: two lines from one vertex crossing a third line can be handled by coordinates or by similar triangles.
solutions.elegant: Triangle $AEF$ is the square minus three right triangles: $144 - 24 - 24 - 36 = 60$. From the similar pairs, $AP/AE = \tfrac34$ and $AQ/AF = \tfrac23$, and triangles sharing angle $A$ have area proportional to the product of the sides along it, so $[APQ] = \tfrac34 \cdot \tfrac23 \cdot 60 = 30$.
